summary: The Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District Boundary Expansion and Partnership Act of 2026 expands the geographic boundaries of the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District into new counties in Virginia and West Virginia, updates its administration, authorizes specific appropriations, and requires a report on replicating its partnership model.

affected_groups.effect: Their localities (Rockbridge County, Virginia; and Berkeley, Jefferson, and Morgan Counties, West Virginia) are added to the National Historic District, and land and interests in land may be acquired from willing sellers.
affected_groups.group: Residents and property owners in newly added counties

affected_groups.effect: Receives authorized annual appropriations of $1,250,000 for operations and maintenance, $2,500,000 annually from 2027 to 2033 for grants, technical assistance, and land acquisition, and guaranteed baseline funding matching fiscal year 2026 levels.

key_provisions: Expands the District's boundaries into Rockbridge County, Virginia, and Berkeley, Jefferson, and Morgan Counties, West Virginia.
Managed by the management entity as a distinct National Historic District partnership model, updating plans for the newly added areas.
Exempts the District from administrative provisions and funding formulas of the National Heritage Area System.

Guarantees that the District and management entity receive at least the same level of funding for management and administration in fiscal year 2027 and thereafter as they did in 2026, and remain eligible for technical assistance and grants.
Authorizes $1,250,000 annually starting in fiscal year 2027, split evenly between operations and the operation/maintenance of battlefield parks, visitor facilities, and preserved historic properties.
Authorizes $2,500,000 annually from fiscal years 2027 through 2033 for grants, technical assistance, and acquiring land from willing sellers.
Requires the Secretary of the Interior to submit a report to Congress within 2 years recommending methods to replicate the District's partnership model in other National Park System locations.
missing_information: Exact maps or descriptions of specific parcels beyond the named counties.
The identity of the management entity.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District Boundary Expansion and Partnership Act of 2026 expands the geographic boundaries of the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District into new counties in Virginia and West Virginia, updates its administration, authorizes specific appropriations, and requires a report on replicating its partnership model.
summary_detail.significance: This bill alters federal historic preservation policy by expanding a designated multi-state historic district, setting dedicated multi-year funding authorizations up to $2,500,000 annually through 2033, and prompting a national review of its partnership model for potential use elsewhere in the National Park System.
